provisioning:The fishermen's stand.name: The fishermen's stand
provisioning:The fishermen's stand.teaser: Cavalaire's day boats sell on Quai Marc Pajot from about ten: the soup fish first, the bream if you're quick
provisioning:The fishermen's stand.story: For a cook the stand is a shopping list written by the sea. Come with a cool bag and two plans: rockfish for a soupe de roche if the small boats worked the rocks, a bream or bass to grill whole if they went further out. Let the fishermen make up the soup mix, since they know which fish give body. Then plan the menu around what you carried away.
provisioning:The fishermen's stand.why: Ask for a soup mix of girelle, rascasse and chapon: the one thing a fish counter in town never assembles for you.
facts: Girelle, rascasse and chapon for soupe de roche; sea bream, sea bass or red mullet; sometimes a spider crab or a langouste
Most mornings from about 10am until sold out, weather and catch permitting (seen Jul 2026)
No booking: some mornings there is nothing

provisioning:Wednesday market.name: Wednesday market
provisioning:Wednesday market.teaser: Place Jean Moulin on a Wednesday morning: a galley's worth of tapenade, honey, cheese and rosé in one square
provisioning:Wednesday market.story: Shop it like a larder run, not a stroll. Walk all hundred-odd stalls once, then come back for the jars: tapenade and anchoïade keep for days on board. The honey seller brings rosemary, lavender, thyme and chestnut honeys from the Maures; taste the chestnut, which is dark and bitter. Leave the fruit and cheese for last so nothing bruises or sweats in the bag.
provisioning:Wednesday market.why: Buy the chestnut honey of the Maures: it tastes of the hills behind the town and travels well.
facts: Tapenade and anchoïade, olives, olive oil, Maures honey, cheese, charcuterie, seasonal fruit and a gulf rosé
No booking: walk in before ten for the best choice

provisioning:La Croix-Valmer's Sunday ma.name: La Croix-Valmer Sunday market
provisioning:La Croix-Valmer's Sunday ma.teaser: Every Sunday morning, all year, La Croix-Valmer's market fills the Place des Palmiers and the street below
provisioning:La Croix-Valmer's Sunday ma.story: When Cavalaire's own market is days away, the Sunday answer is one village east. The Provençal market of La Croix-Valmer sets up on the Place des Palmiers every Sunday morning of the year and runs on towards the Rue du Train des Pignes, with between about 80 and 170 stallholders depending on the season, from the gulf, the Var and the wider region. Look for olives, herbs, summer peaches and bottles from the estates on the hills around the village. In summer there is also a Thursday evening craft market.
provisioning:La Croix-Valmer's Sunday ma.why: The one full market of the week within reach on a Sunday, and it trades in winter too.
facts: Morning only; no fixed closing time is published, so do not count on it after about 1pm
Early, before the car parks fill in summer
Olives, herbs, peaches in season and local wine from the estates of the peninsula

provisioning:Domaine de la Croix.name: Domaine de la Croix
provisioning:Domaine de la Croix.teaser: A classified Côtes de Provence growth at La Croix-Valmer, with a seaside organic sister under another label
provisioning:Domaine de la Croix.story: Founded in 1882, Domaine de la Croix is one of the estates named in the 1955 Cru Classé list (its own card is under Drink). The cellar shop sits on Boulevard de Tabarin, inland from Gigaro. The estate also farms Bastide Blanche, its certified-organic vines on sandy ground between Cap Lardier and Cap Taillat, sold under their own label. For the galley, the Irrésistible range comes as a rosé and as a white; taste both against the Bastide Blanche rosé before you load cases.
provisioning:Domaine de la Croix.why: Buy one bottle each of La Croix and Bastide Blanche and taste schist against sand side by side.
facts: Listed as open daily year-round in 2026 tourism listings; the old guide gave Monday to Saturday, 10am to 1pm and 3pm to 7.30pm (seen Jul 2026); call ahead in winter
The Irrésistible rosé and white, the Cru Classé wines, the organic Bastide Blanche rosé

provisioning:Domaine La Tourraque.name: Domaine La Tourraque
provisioning:Domaine La Tourraque.teaser: A Ramatuelle family farm since 1805, its vines inside the protected land of the three capes
provisioning:Domaine La Tourraque.story: La Tourraque lies in a valley behind Cap Taillat, on land classified as a protected site in 1995 and now part of the Port-Cros national park's area. The family says it has worked this ground since 1805, first as a farm that fed itself from fruit, cereals, olives, hunting and fishing, until the vine took over. Today Sébastien Craveris Brun and his brother Guillaume are taking over from the older generation, and the wines have been certified organic since the 2013 vintage. Tasting at the cellar is free and needs no appointment.
provisioning:Domaine La Tourraque.why: A free tasting at a family cellar a few minutes' drive from the Cap Taillat path.
facts: 2444 chemin de la Bastide Blanche Sud, Ramatuelle
October to March, Monday to Friday 10am to noon and 2pm to 5pm, closed weekends; April to September, Monday to Friday 10am to 6pm and Saturday 10am to 2pm (Oct 2026; listings disagree, phone first)
Organic AOC Côtes de Provence rosé, white and red

provisioning:Château Minuty.name: Château Minuty
provisioning:Château Minuty.teaser: The Gassin estate behind the gulf's best-known pale rosé, now part of Moët Hennessy
provisioning:Château Minuty.story: Château Minuty, at Gassin on the hill above the gulf, is another of the 1955 Crus Classés (see the Drink card). For decades it was the Matton family's house; in February 2023 Moët Hennessy, the wine and spirits arm of LVMH, took a majority stake, with Jean-Étienne and François Matton staying on to run it, Decanter reported. It now makes several million bottles of rosé a year. Entry to the tasting cellar is free, and the shop also sells online with click and collect.
provisioning:Château Minuty.why: Taste the top cuvées at the source before deciding whether the label is worth the price on board.
facts: Winter hours (October to 1 April): Monday to Friday 9am to 12.30pm and 1.30pm to 6pm, closed weekends; summer (May to September) daily 9am to 7pm, per the 2025-26 listings; the 2026-27 schedule was not posted in Oct 2026
Côtes de Provence Cru Classé rosés, also white and red

provisioning:La Cave de Mon Village.name: La Cave de Mon Village
provisioning:La Cave de Mon Village.teaser: The town's caviste with a counter: Provençal rosés, small local estates, a cheese board and a glass
provisioning:La Cave de Mon Village.story: On the Avenue des Alliés, a short walk up from the beach, this is the in-town shop for restocking the boat's rosé without driving to the estates. The shelves lean towards fresh Provençal rosés and lesser-known domaines of the area, with aged cheeses and house-made nibbles at the counter, and now and then a producer pouring a tasting. It is a caviste first, not a natural-wine specialist: come for a reliable local bottle and a glass after the beach.
provisioning:La Cave de Mon Village.why: Ask for the small local estates you have not seen in the supermarket: that is what the shop is for.
facts: Seven days, 9am to 1pm and 3.30pm to 7.30pm (seen Jul 2026; not confirmed in Oct 2026)
Provençal rosés from small local estates, aged cheeses, house-made nibbles, a glass at the counter

walks:Le Sentier des Trois Caps.name: Le Sentier des Trois Caps
walks:Le Sentier des Trois Caps.teaser: From Gigaro to Cap Taillat and back through the cork oaks: the longest wild shore left on the peninsula
walks:Le Sentier des Trois Caps.story: Start at the eastern end of Gigaro beach, where the sand gives way to rock and the yellow marks of the coastal path begin. The path is the old customs track, cut along the shore so that patrols could watch every cove, and it still goes where they went: up over Cap Lardier, down to the long Briande bay, on to the sand neck of Cap Taillat. From there the loop turns inland and climbs back through cork oak, pine and cistus. What the walk shows is a boundary: the villas stop where the Conservatoire du littoral's land begins, and from there to Taillat there is almost nothing built. The third cape, Camarat with its lighthouse, stays ahead of you on the Ramatuelle side.
walks:Le Sentier des Trois Caps.why: The only way to see this shore whole is on foot; leave the beach day for the coves you pass.
facts: Plage de Gigaro, eastern end, La Croix-Valmer
About 14 km for the full loop, coast out and forest track back
About 4 hours of walking; most people make a day of it with swims
Yellow-marked coastal path, rocky and steep in places, then wide forest tracks inland
Set out early; in summer the massif can be closed to walkers on high fire-risk days, so check the prefecture's daily access map
Cap Lardier's crest, the douaniers' coves and the Briande beach, each with its own card
Plenty of water (there is nothing to buy on the path), proper shoes, a mask and swim things

walks:Cap Lardier's crest.name: Cap Lardier's crest
walks:Cap Lardier's crest.teaser: Mid-walk, the cape's high point opens a half-circle of sea from Camarat's lighthouse to the Îles d'Hyères
walks:Cap Lardier's crest.story: Cap Lardier was classified as a protected site in 1966, and from 1978 the Conservatoire du littoral bought its pine massif, about 300 hectares, parcel by parcel. The result is the longest protected stretch of shore of the three capes, some 6 km, and from the crest you take it in at once: the Camarat lighthouse to the east, Cap Taillat's low headland below, the Îles du Levant and the other Îles d'Hyères offshore, and the whole bay of Cavalaire behind you. The Bastide Blanche and La Croix vines run almost to the cliff edge. There is no road to the point.
walks:Cap Lardier's crest.why: The one place on the walk where you see why the capes stayed empty: green on one side, built on every other.
facts: Plage de Gigaro, La Croix-Valmer, on the Trois Caps path
Roughly an hour on foot from Gigaro
Rocky coastal path with steep climbs
Morning, before the heat and with the light behind you over the islands
The view east to the Camarat lighthouse

walks:Sentier du Fenouillet.name: Sentier du Fenouillet
walks:Sentier du Fenouillet.teaser: Cavalaire's own headland walk: cork oak, strawberry trees and coves, from Bonporteau beach on foot
walks:Sentier du Fenouillet.story: The Fenouillet headland is the Domaine Foncin. In 1977 Mireille Foncin, daughter of the geographer Pierre Foncin, a founder of the Alliance Française, left the land to the Conservatoire du littoral, one of the first gifts it ever received, and that is why this piece of the Corniche des Maures has no villas. The path leaves Plage de Bonporteau, follows the cliffs towards Pointe du Dattier with views to the Îles d'Hyères and back to Cap Lardier, then returns through a shaded, damp valley. Come in autumn: the strawberry trees flower and fruit at the same time, and the maquis smells of honey.
walks:Sentier du Fenouillet.why: No car needed: the maquis of the Maures begins on the edge of town.
facts: Short loops of about 3 to 4.5 km; the full circuit to Le Dattier about 8 km
About 3 hours for the full circuit
Signposted coastal path, narrow and steep in places with some scrambly sea-edge sections; about 360 m of climbing on the full circuit
Morning, or late afternoon in autumn when the strawberry trees are in fruit
The cove stops below the path and the island view from the high points

calas:Cap Taillat.name: Cap Taillat
calas:Cap Taillat.teaser: A rocky headland tied to the shore by a lane of sand, with a different bay breaking on each side
calas:Cap Taillat.story: Cap Taillat was once an island. The currents built a tombolo, a strip of fine sand no wider than a lane, that now ties it to the mainland, with the Baie de Briande on the La Croix-Valmer side and the Baie de Bonporteau (Ramatuelle's, not Cavalaire's) on the other. Wind from east or west moves the sand constantly and winter storms eat at it, so the dune is fenced with chestnut ganivelles. The Conservatoire du littoral owns some 142 hectares here. On 24 July 2017 a fire ran from Gigaro to L'Escalet and burned the cape to ash; after about 2,000 dead trees were felled the path reopened eight months later on a new line. The maquis came back fast; the umbrella pines will take decades.
calas:Cap Taillat.why: Stand on the sand neck and swim on whichever side the wind is not blowing.
facts: On foot only: the shortest walk in is from the Plage de l'Escalet car park, Ramatuelle; or the long coastal path from Gigaro; or by sea
Early morning, before the walkers arrive from L'Escalet
Water, shade and a mask; there are no cafés, no lifeguard and no facilities
The old customs house at the start of the tombolo

calas:Plage de la Briande.name: Plage de la Briande
calas:Plage de la Briande.teaser: La Croix-Valmer's wildest beach: a long curve of sand with pines behind it and no road in
calas:Plage de la Briande.story: Briande is the last beach of La Croix-Valmer, a long curve of pale sand on the western flank of Cap Taillat, backed by thick maquis and umbrella pines with nothing built behind it. No road reaches it, so the only way in is the coastal path, about 45 minutes on foot from the southern car park at L'Escalet, and it lies inside the protected Lardier and Taillat corridor, which means it will never be built on or serviced. On a weekday out of August you can have a stretch of it to yourself. Naturists use the wild coves along the walk, but Briande is not an official naturist beach: read the signs.
calas:Plage de la Briande.why: The long walk in keeps the crowds down; that is the whole point of the place.
facts: On foot, about 45 minutes on the coastal path from the L'Escalet car park, Ramatuelle, or the longer way from Gigaro; by sea
Morning, when the water is flat and the sand still cool
Water, food and shade; there is nothing on the beach
The view across the bay to the Cap Taillat neck

calas:The douaniers' coves.name: The douaniers' coves
calas:The douaniers' coves.teaser: Three coves on the customs path from Gigaro: the tiny Douane, Jovat with its ruined cabin, and wild Brouis
calas:The douaniers' coves.story: Leave Gigaro by its quiet eastern corner and the coastal path begins to thread small coves most visitors never learn the names of. First the crique de la Douane, tiny and close to the start. Then Jovat, sandier, with the ruins of an old fishing cabin above the water. Then Brouis, the wildest, where you are more or less certain to be alone. All three sit on protected land and in a Natura 2000 zone, which is why they stay calm even in August while Gigaro fills. The path itself is the Trois Caps walk, under its own card.
calas:The douaniers' coves.why: Walk past the first cove; the farther you go, the emptier the sand.
facts: On foot from the eastern end of Plage de Gigaro, La Croix-Valmer, on the yellow-marked coastal path; about 4.4 km one way to Cap Lardier, steep in places
Morning, before the heat on the path
Sturdy shoes, water and a mask
Brouis, the last and least visited of the three
calas:The douaniers' coves.maps_query: Plage de Gigaro, La Croix-Valmer, Var, France

calas:Bonporteau.name: Bonporteau
calas:Bonporteau.teaser: Cavalaire's wild cove, with a free buoyed snorkel trail laid over the seagrass just offshore
calas:Bonporteau.story: A steep footpath from the Avenue de Bonporteau drops through eucalyptus and palms to a cove of fine sand ringed with rock and tamarisk, with picnic tables in the pine shade. Just offshore, seven coloured buoys and underwater panels mark a snorkel trail over the Posidonia meadows, the nursery of this coast, where saupes, bream and girelles drift and a young grouper sometimes hangs under a ledge. It lies in the marine area of the Port-Cros national park and is free to anyone who can swim with mask and fins. In summer a state-qualified guide leads it; the park's guided mornings have been on Tuesdays. The buoys are in from June to September, so in late October the trail is closed for the year.
calas:Bonporteau.why: A free underwater trail on the edge of town, unsupervised and quiet while the main beach fills.
facts: On foot down a steep path from Avenue de Bonporteau, Cavalaire; no cars to the beach
Morning, when the water is clearest and the light reaches the seabed
Mask, snorkel and fins (not supplied), water; there is no lifeguard
The guided session, about 1h30 with 35 to 50 minutes in the water, €8 child and €11 adult, booked through the gulf's booking site (Oct 2026 listing; trail open 1 June to 30 September 2026)

calas:The Rayol coves.name: The Rayol coves
calas:The Rayol coves.teaser: White-sand coves under the Corniche des Maures, reached by paths steep enough to keep them wild
calas:The Rayol coves.story: West of Cavalaire the Massif des Maures drops almost straight into the sea, and the coast road strings small pine-backed beaches between the Rayol and Le Lavandou: Le Rayol, Le Canadel, Cavalière, Pramousquier. Between them hide smaller coves such as the Plage du Figuier, white sand and clear water over rock and seagrass, reached by steep and sometimes unmarked paths that locals call sportif. The slope is the protection. In autumn and winter you may find the sand lined with brown banks of dead Posidonia leaves; they are a sign of a healthy seabed, not a dirty beach, and they protect the sand from storms.
calas:The Rayol coves.why: Greener and far less built-up than the club beaches east of the peninsula, ten to twenty minutes by car.
facts: By the coast road west from Cavalaire towards Le Lavandou, then on foot down steep paths; some coves have no marked access
Morning, before the corniche car parks fill
Shoes for the path, mask and fins, water
Plage du Figuier, beside the Domaine du Rayol

calas:Le Sentier Marin du Rayol.name: Le Sentier Marin du Rayol
calas:Le Sentier Marin du Rayol.teaser: A guided snorkel over the seagrass of the Baie du Figuier, from the Domaine du Rayol's own beach
calas:Le Sentier Marin du Rayol.story: Below the Domaine du Rayol the bay of the Figuier is protected land and sea, and in summer the estate runs a guided snorkel over it in wetsuit, mask and fins. The guide takes small groups over Posidonia meadows, urchins and damselfish, and with luck an octopus. The one thing to carry home: Posidonia is not a seaweed but a flowering plant that grows under the sea, a great oxygen maker and the nursery for much of what you see. The 2026 season ran from 18 June to 13 September, so it reopens next June; the garden itself has its own card under Culture.
calas:Le Sentier Marin du Rayol.why: The easiest way to see the seabed of the Hyères islands without leaving the mainland.
facts: Domaine du Rayol, Rayol-Canadel-sur-Mer, on the coast road west of Cavalaire
The first session of the morning, when the bay is calmest
Swimwear and a towel; wetsuit, mask and fins are provided; the swimmer must be 8 or over and able to swim
Booking: about 2 hours with 45 minutes in the water, three to six sessions a day mid-June to mid-September; from €37 adult with garden entry included (seen Jul 2026; 2026 price not confirmed)

avoid:Saint-Tropez by car in August.name: Saint-Tropez by car in August
avoid:Saint-Tropez by car in August.teaser: Seventeen kilometres on the map, half a day in a queue on the beach roads in high summer
avoid:Saint-Tropez by car in August.story: Saint-Tropez looks close from Cavalaire, about 17 km, and in August that is the trap: the peninsula's roads clog at beach time and the day goes in traffic rather than in the village. The old advice to take a Bateaux Verts shuttle from Cavalaire's quay no longer holds: their 2026 lines run to Saint-Tropez from Sainte-Maxime, Port Grimaud, Les Marines de Cogolin and Les Issambres, not from Cavalaire. From Cavalaire's port, the Vedettes Îles d'Or ran seasonal coastal trips towards Saint-Tropez from May to late September 2026, an excursion rather than a ferry line.
avoid:Saint-Tropez by car in August.why: In August, go by sea or go at dawn; use the car for the western corniche instead.
facts: In high summer, a solid line of cars on the peninsula roads at beach hour
Arrive by tender or a seasonal boat, or drive at dawn or dusk; keep the car for the Corniche des Maures towards Rayol-Canadel and Le Lavandou, where the road flows

avoid:The Pampelonne fantasy.name: The Pampelonne fantasy
avoid:The Pampelonne fantasy.teaser: The famous club beaches are on the far side of the peninsula, a summer drive and a three-figure sunbed away
avoid:The Pampelonne fantasy.story: Pampelonne's club beaches sit on the eastern side of the peninsula, beyond Ramatuelle. From Cavalaire in summer that can mean an hour of traffic each way, then a sunbed priced in three figures. The local beach day is closer and costs nothing: Cavalaire's own bay of sand, more than 2 km long, and the protected coves under Cap Lardier and around Gigaro, a short hop east, where nothing has been built and nothing is for rent.
avoid:The Pampelonne fantasy.why: Spend the hour you save walking to a cove you will share with almost nobody.
facts: Paid mattresses in rows and a long drive to reach them
Cavalaire's long town beach, or the coves below Cap Lardier and the Briande beach, each with its own card

avoid:Reading the winter seafront as emp.name: The winter seafront
avoid:Reading the winter seafront as emp.teaser: Shuttered terraces in winter do not mean there is nothing here: the town's larder keeps going
avoid:Reading the winter seafront as emp.story: From late October the beach restaurants and most summer terraces close, and by January the seafront looks shut and the port is quiet. That is the resort sleeping, not the town. The Wednesday market on Place Jean Moulin trades all year, the fishermen still sell on the quay on mornings when the boats have been out, the Domaine du Rayol garden stays open on winter hours, and in February the mimosa turns the corniche yellow.
avoid:Reading the winter seafront as emp.why: Out of season the market and the quay are the reasons to come, and you will not queue for either.
facts: Closed beach restaurants and empty terraces along the seafront, more so each week from now to January
Plan around Wednesday morning's market and a morning at the fishermen's stand, add the Rayol garden, and come back in February for the mimosa

avoid:'Fresh fish' without asking.name: ‘Fresh fish’ without asking
avoid:'Fresh fish' without asking.teaser: A seafront menu that says fresh fish may be serving frozen catch at summer prices
avoid:'Fresh fish' without asking.story: Plenty of resort tables put frozen fish on the plate at high-season prices, a few minutes' walk from boats that landed real fish that morning. The fix is two questions. Where did it come from, and when? A kitchen that buys from the Cavalaire boats will tell you the name of the fish and the morning it came in. Note that the quay sale is a direct stand, not a criée auction, whatever the old menus say.
avoid:'Fresh fish' without asking.why: Ask where the fish came from; a straight answer is the best guide to the kitchen.
facts: Grilled 'fresh' fish at seafront prices, with no species or boat named
Buy the day's catch at the fishermen's stand on Quai Marc Pajot in the morning (bream, bass, rascasse for soup), or ask a restaurant which boat its fish came off

follow:Cavalaire Tourisme.name: Cavalaire Tourisme
follow:Cavalaire Tourisme.teaser: The town's tourist office: beach conditions, market days and what is actually open this week
follow:Cavalaire Tourisme.story: Cavalaire's official tourist office, at the Maison de la Mer by the seafront, is the first place to check what is open, above all in the shoulder months when restaurants close one by one. Its Instagram account, @cavalairetourisme, and its website carry beach conditions, the summer programme of concerts and festivals, market days and the town's events calendar. In late October it is also where the end-of-season closing dates appear first.
follow:Cavalaire Tourisme.why: In October, the quickest way to know which tables and services are still working.
facts: The official tourist office of Cavalaire-sur-Mer; Instagram @cavalairetourisme
French, with an English section on the website
The agenda, beach information and the practical pages on markets and opening seasons

follow:Golfe de Saint-Tropez Tourisme.name: Golfe de Saint-Tropez Tourisme
follow:Golfe de Saint-Tropez Tourisme.teaser: The gulf's community tourist office, for the wider agenda of markets, sea shuttles and big fixtures
follow:Golfe de Saint-Tropez Tourisme.story: The Office de Tourisme Communautaire du Golfe de Saint-Tropez, based in Cogolin, covers the inland and western communes of the gulf, Le Rayol-Canadel among them, and carries the Vignobles et Découvertes wine-tourism label. Follow it on Instagram as @otc_golfedesainttropez for the gulf-wide agenda: markets, summer sea shuttles, estate events and the big fixtures such as Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez. Cavalaire itself keeps its own office.
follow:Golfe de Saint-Tropez Tourisme.why: One feed for what is on across the gulf, beyond Cavalaire's own calendar.
facts: The intercommunal tourist office of the Gulf of Saint-Tropez; Instagram @otc_golfedesainttropez

follow:Les Bateaux Verts.name: Les Bateaux Verts
follow:Les Bateaux Verts.teaser: The Sainte-Maxime boat company whose green shuttles cross the gulf to Saint-Tropez
follow:Les Bateaux Verts.story: Les Bateaux Verts, based in Sainte-Maxime, run the gulf's sea shuttles about ten months a year, seven days a week, with one to four crossings an hour to Saint-Tropez from Sainte-Maxime, Port Grimaud, Les Marines de Cogolin and Les Issambres; in 2026 they added round-the-clock crossings from Sainte-Maxime at the height of summer, weather permitting. Their 2026 timetable lists no Cavalaire stop, so from here the account is useful once you are on the far side of the gulf. Follow @bateaux_verts for season starts and timetable changes.
follow:Les Bateaux Verts.why: The car-free way into Saint-Tropez in August, once you reach one of their quays.
facts: The gulf's shuttle-boat operator, Sainte-Maxime; Instagram @bateaux_verts; no Cavalaire departures listed in 2026
The yearly timetable and fares brochure, and weather cancellations

follow:Parc national de Port-Cros.name: Parc national de Port-Cros
follow:Parc national de Port-Cros.teaser: The national park behind the protected capes and marine trails of this coast
follow:Parc national de Port-Cros.story: The Parc national de Port-Cros manages the islands of Port-Cros and Porquerolles and works with the communes of the mainland coast, including the Cap Lardier and Cap Taillat shore and Cavalaire's marine area. Its account, @parcnationaldeportcros, posts trail news, wildlife and the summer programme of guided outings, and its website publishes downloadable sheets for each walk and snorkel trail, with maps and rules.
follow:Parc national de Port-Cros.why: The source for why this coast stayed wild and for the rules when you anchor or walk in it.
facts: The national park authority for the Hyères islands and the protected coast around Cavalaire; Instagram @parcnationaldeportcros
The trail and snorkel-trail sheets and the summer guided-outings programme

follow:Domaine du Rayol.name: Domaine du Rayol
follow:Domaine du Rayol.teaser: The Rayol garden's own feed: seasonal hours, concerts and the summer snorkel trail
follow:Domaine du Rayol.story: The Domaine du Rayol, at neighbouring Rayol-Canadel, posts its opening hours, events and the dates of its summer guided snorkel on @domainedurayol and on its website, where the yearly programme is published as a download. In winter the feed is where changes to the garden's opening hours are announced, and in spring the first booking dates for the Jardin Marin appear there. The garden itself has its own card under Culture.
follow:Domaine du Rayol.why: The quickest way to catch a concert or the first snorkel dates of the season.
facts: The account of the Domaine du Rayol, Jardin des Méditerranées, Rayol-Canadel-sur-Mer; Instagram @domainedurayol
The yearly programme, seasonal hours and the Jardin Marin booking pages
